thread:
ada: Quick heads-up — onboarding Mixtral-7B-8k. After safetensors conversion I'm seeing RoPE scale mismatch and a perf regression in KV-miss path. p95 jumped ~2.1x on production-like load.

jordan: logs? stack traces? any hf_config differences between original and converted artifacts?

ada: attaching minimal dump — kernel chosen is 'rope-rotary-v1' but model was originally served with 'rotary-v2-scale' (we default to v1 when metadata missing). No stack, just latency spike on warm requests.

vikram: could be missing 'rotary_scaling' in hf_config.json or safetensors.metadata.axes/extra. We saw similar once where conversion stripped model.attrs['rope_scale'].

nina: re: conversion — our conversion script does: 
```
python convert_safetensors.py --in mixtral.safetensors --out mixtral.pt --strip-meta
```
strip-meta was used to reduce disk, oops.

sam: that strip-meta flag is the smoking gun. Safetensors may embed 'rope_scale' in metadata; runtime parser falls back to legacy kernel.

ada: @ci-bot ran a quick profile on a local replica:
```
perfctl profile --model mixtral-7b-8k --scenario kv-miss --samples 100
# results: p50=18ms p95=68ms p99=112ms
```
previous baseline (with metadata): p95=31ms.

jordan: so ~2x p95 regression. Does kernel selection logic fall back to non-quantized codepath? that could explain more cycles.

vikram: kernel selection log excerpt: 
```
[INFO] kernel_picker: requested kernels: [rotary-v2-scale, rotary-v2]
[WARN] model_metadata: rotary_scale missing, using rotary-v1 fallback
[INFO] selected_kernel: rope-rotary-v1 (scalar rot)
```
rotary-v1 uses slower vector ops for our head-size/kv-dim combo.

nina: we should also check batching heuristics — fallback kernel doesn't support our packed batch micro-kernel so batcher drops to batch_size=1 for that model, causing throughput erosion under stress.

sam: also noticed KV cache eviction thrash in trace; when batch_size changes, cache alignment mismatches cause frequent KV cache misses -> extra memcpy.

ada: Proposed immediate fixes:
- revert strip-meta in conversion script so safetensors metadata preserved
- update HF parser to read rotary_scaling from both hf_config.json and safetensors metadata (account for old key names)
- add a soft-fail warning instead of silent fallback

jordan: agree. Add a unit test that rejects converted artifacts without rope metadata. Also add a lint step to onboarding that warns on batcher/kernel fallback.

vikram: I'll draft a small patch to parser: detect keys ["rope_scale","rotary_scaling","rotary_scale"], coerce floats, and attach to model.config.metadata. Also add telemetry event kernel_fallback_reason for better triage.

nina: for short-term mitigation we can force kernel selection by model tag (e.g., mixtral-7b-8k:preferred_kernel=rotary-v2-scale) in model registry so canary keeps using optimized kernels while we fix conversion.

sam: perf test plan: canary 5% traffic -> measure p95 and kv-hit-rate. If p95 improves by >20% rollback. I'll set up AB test in bench infra.

ada: CI change: conversion job should run `inspect_safetensors.py --print-meta` and fail if rope metadata absent unless explicitly allowed. I'll make a PR.

vikram: small gotcha — some older HF configs used implicit scaling = head_dim / 64; add heuristic fallback with a small note in logs. But don't let heuristic trigger kernel fallback silently.

jordan: also add a quick profiler metric: kernel_dispatch_time and batcher_adjust_count per model-run. That will help spot batcher thrash.

nina: filed follow-up tasks: D-1234 (parser fix), D-1235 (conversion lint), D-1236 (canary override), D-1237 (perf dashboards).

sam: I'll kick off the canary later today once parser patch lands in staging.

ada: thanks — big win if we avoid perf drop for more customers. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: deploy pipeline triggered: staging/convert-lint-runner v2026.3 -> testing conversion artifact checks.
